raw: CHAPTER XII. Darkness
en: [Chapter 12] Darkness

raw: Sydney Carton paused in the street, not quite decided where to go. “At Tellson’s banking-house at nine,” he said, with a musing face. “Shall I do well, in the mean time, to show myself?
en: Sydney Carton paused in the street, not quite sure where to go next. “At Tellson's Bank at nine,” he said with a thoughtful face. “Would it be a good idea to show myself in the meantime?
ko: 시드니 카턴은 다음으로 어디로 가야 할지 확신이 서지 않아 거리에서 멈춰 섰다. “아홉 시에 텔슨 은행에서,” 그는 생각에 잠긴 얼굴로 말했다. “그동안 내 모습을 보여주는 것이 좋은 생각일까?

raw: I think so.
en: I think so.
ko: 나는 그렇게 생각한다.

raw: It is best that these people should know there is such a man as I here; it is a sound precaution, and may be a necessary preparation.
en: It is best that these people know there is someone here who looks like Charles. It is a smart precaution, and it might be a necessary step.
ko: 이 사람들이 찰스와 닮은 누군가가 여기에 있다는 것을 아는 것이 최선이다. 그것은 현명한 예방 조치이며, 필요한 단계일 수도 있다.

raw: But care, care, care!
en: But I must be careful, careful, careful!
ko: 하지만 나는 조심하고, 조심하고, 또 조심해야 한다!

raw: Let me think it out!”
en: Let me think this through!”
ko: 끝까지 철저하게 생각해보자!”

raw: Checking his steps which had begun to tend towards an object, he took a turn or two in the already darkening street, and traced the thought in his mind to its possible consequences.
en: Stopping himself from walking too quickly toward his destination, he paced up and down the darkening street, tracing his plan to its possible consequences.
ko: 목적지를 향해 너무 빨리 걷는 것을 멈추고, 그는 어두워지는 거리를 이리저리 오가며 자신의 계획이 가져올 수 있는 결과들을 추적해 보았다.

raw: His first impression was confirmed. “It is best,” he said, finally resolved, “that these people should know there is such a man as I here.” And he turned his face towards Saint Antoine.
en: His first instinct was confirmed. “It is best,” he decided at last, “that these people know someone like me is here.” And he turned toward the neighborhood of Saint Antoine.
ko: 그의 첫 번째 직감이 확인되었다. “최선이다,” 마침내 그는 결정을 내렸다, “이 사람들이 나와 같은 누군가가 여기에 있다는 것을 아는 것이.” 그리고 그는 생탕투안 동네를 향해 돌아섰다.

raw: Defarge had described himself, that day, as the keeper of a wine-shop in the Saint Antoine suburb.
en: Defarge had described himself in court that day as a wine-shop owner in Saint Antoine.
ko: 드파르지는 그날 법정에서 자신을 생탕투안의 와인 가게 주인이라고 설명했었다.

raw: It was not difficult for one who knew the city well, to find his house without asking any question.
en: For someone who knew Paris well, it was not hard to find the shop without asking directions.
ko: 파리를 잘 아는 사람에게는 길을 묻지 않고도 가게를 찾는 것이 어렵지 않았다.

raw: Having ascertained its situation, Carton came out of those closer streets again, and dined at a place of refreshment and fell sound asleep after dinner.
en: Once he located it, Carton left the narrow streets, ate dinner at a small restaurant, and fell fast asleep afterward.
ko: 일단 그것을 찾자, 카턴은 좁은 거리들을 떠나 작은 식당에서 저녁을 먹고 그 후에 깊이 잠들었다.

raw: For the first time in many years, he had no strong drink.
en: For the first time in many years, he did not touch any hard alcohol.
ko: 수년 만에 처음으로, 그는 독한 술에 전혀 손을 대지 않았다.

raw: Since last night he had taken nothing but a little light thin wine, and last night he had dropped the brandy slowly down on Mr.
en: Since the night before, he had drunk nothing but a little light wine, and last night he had poured his brandy onto Mr.
ko: 전날 밤부터 그는 가벼운 와인 조금 외에는 아무것도 마시지 않았고, 어젯밤에는 그의 브랜디를 미스터

raw: Lorry’s hearth like a man who had done with it.
en: Lorry's hearth, like a man who was finished with drinking for good.
ko: 로리의 난로에 부어버렸다, 영원히 술을 끊은 사람처럼.

raw: It was as late as seven o’clock when he awoke refreshed, and went out into the streets again.
en: It was seven o'clock when he woke up feeling refreshed and went back out into the streets.
ko: 그가 개운함을 느끼며 깨어나 다시 거리로 나갔을 때는 일곱 시였다.

raw: As he passed along towards Saint Antoine, he stopped at a shop-window where there was a mirror, and slightly altered the disordered arrangement of his loose cravat, and his coat-collar, and his wild hair.
en: On his way to Saint Antoine, he stopped at a shop window with a mirror and adjusted his messy tie, his coat collar, and his wild hair.
ko: 생탕투안으로 가는 길에, 그는 거울이 있는 상점 진열장 앞에 멈춰 서서 지저분한 넥타이, 코트 깃, 그리고 헝클어진 머리를 정돈했다.

raw: This done, he went on direct to Defarge’s, and went in.
en: Once he was presentable, he walked straight to Defarge's wine-shop and went inside.
ko: 일단 그가 단정해지자, 그는 똑바로 드파르지의 와인 가게로 걸어가 안으로 들어갔다.

raw: There happened to be no customer in the shop but Jacques Three, of the restless fingers and the croaking voice.
en: There were no customers in the shop except Jacques Three, the man with the twitchy fingers and the croaking voice.
ko: 경련하는 손가락과 쉰 목소리를 가진 자크 삼세를 제외하고는 가게에 손님이 없었다.

raw: This man, whom he had seen upon the Jury, stood drinking at the little counter, in conversation with the Defarges, man and wife.
en: This man, whom Carton had seen on the jury, stood drinking at the small counter, talking with Monsieur and Madame Defarge.
ko: 카턴이 배심원단에서 보았던 이 남자는 작은 카운터에서 술을 마시며 무슈와 마담 드파르지와 이야기를 나누고 서 있었다.

raw: The Vengeance assisted in the conversation, like a regular member of the establishment.
en: The Vengeance also joined in the conversation as if she were a regular employee.
ko: 복수도 마치 정규 직원인 것처럼 대화에 참여했다.

raw: As Carton walked in, took his seat and asked (in very indifferent French) for a small measure of wine, Madame Defarge cast a careless glance at him, and then a keener, and then a keener, and then advanced to him herself, and asked him what it was he had ordered.
en: When Carton walked in, sat down, and asked in very poor French for a small glass of wine, Madame Defarge glanced at him carelessly. Then she looked closer, and even closer, before walking over to him herself to ask what he had ordered.
ko: 카턴이 걸어 들어와 앉아서 매우 서투른 프랑스어로 작은 와인 한 잔을 주문했을 때, 마담 드파르지는 무심하게 그를 힐끗 보았다. 그러고 나서 그녀는 그가 무엇을 주문했는지 묻기 위해 직접 그에게 다가가기 전에 더 가까이, 그리고 더욱 가까이서 바라보았다.

raw: He repeated what he had already said.
en: He repeated his order.
ko: 그는 주문을 반복했다.

raw: “English?” asked Madame Defarge, inquisitively raising her dark eyebrows.
en: “Are you English?” asked Madame Defarge, raising her dark eyebrows curiously.
ko: “당신은 영국인입니까?” 마담 드파르지가 호기심에 찬 어두운 눈썹을 치켜올리며 물었다.

raw: After looking at her, as if the sound of even a single French word were slow to express itself to him, he answered, in his former strong foreign accent. “Yes, madame, yes.
en: He looked at her as if it took him a long time to understand even a single French word, then answered in a thick English accent. “Yes, madame, yes.
ko: 그는 단 하나의 프랑스어 단어조차 이해하는 데 오랜 시간이 걸린다는 듯이 그녀를 바라보다가, 짙은 영국 억양으로 대답했다. “네, 마담, 네.

raw: I am English!”
en: I am English!”
ko: 나는 영국인입니다!”

raw: Madame Defarge returned to her counter to get the wine, and, as he took up a Jacobin journal and feigned to pore over it puzzling out its meaning, he heard her say, “I swear to you, like Evrémonde!”
en: Madame Defarge went back to her counter to pour the wine. As he picked up a revolutionary newspaper and pretended to struggle through reading it, he heard her whisper, “I swear to you, he looks just like Evrémonde!”
ko: 마담 드파르지는 와인을 따르기 위해 그녀의 카운터로 돌아갔다. 그가 혁명 신문을 집어 들고 애써 읽으려 노력하는 척할 때, 그는 그녀가 속삭이는 것을 들었다. “맹세컨대, 그는 정확히 에브레몽드처럼 생겼어요!”

raw: Defarge brought him the wine, and gave him Good Evening.
en: Defarge brought him the wine and said good evening.
ko: 드파르지가 그에게 와인을 가져다주며 저녁 인사를 건넸다.

raw: “How?”
en: “What?”
ko: “뭐라고요?”

raw: “Good evening.”
en: “Good evening.”
ko: “좋은 저녁입니다.”

raw: “Oh!
en: “Oh!

raw: Good evening, citizen,” filling his glass. “Ah! and good wine.
en: Good evening, citizen,” Carton said, filling his glass. “Ah, and good wine.
ko: 좋은 저녁입니다, 시민,” 카턴이 잔을 채우며 말했다. “아, 그리고 좋은 와인이군요.

raw: I drink to the Republic.”
en: I drink to the Republic.”
ko: 공화국을 위해 마시겠습니다.”

raw: Defarge went back to the counter, and said, “Certainly, a little like.”  Madame sternly retorted, “I tell you a good deal like.” Jacques Three pacifically remarked, “He is so much in your mind, see you, madame.”  The amiable Vengeance added, with a laugh, “Yes, my faith!
en: Defarge went back to the counter and said, “He does look a little like him.” Madame Defarge snapped back, “I tell you, he looks a lot like him!” Jacques Three calmly remarked, “He is on your mind so much, you see, madame.” The Vengeance laughed and added, “Yes, indeed!
ko: 드파르지는 카운터로 돌아가서 말했다. “그는 약간 그와 닮았어.” 마담 드파르지가 쏘아붙였다. “내가 말했잖아, 그와 많이 닮았다고!” 자크 3세가 차분하게 평했다. “마담, 당신 마음속에 그가 너무 많이 있어서 그렇습니다.” 복수가 웃으며 덧붙였다. “예, 정말로요!

raw: And you are looking forward with so much pleasure to seeing him once more to-morrow!”
en: And you are looking forward so much to seeing Evrémonde one last time tomorrow!”
ko: 그리고 당신은 내일 에브레몽드를 마지막으로 보는 것을 너무나 고대하고 있잖아요!”

raw: Carton followed the lines and words of his paper, with a slow forefinger, and with a studious and absorbed face.
en: Carton followed the lines of the newspaper with his finger, looking completely focused and absorbed.
ko: 카턴은 손가락으로 신문의 줄을 따라가며 완전히 집중하고 몰두한 것처럼 보였다.

raw: They were all leaning their arms on the counter close together, speaking low.
en: The group at the counter leaned close together, speaking quietly.
ko: 카운터에 있던 그룹은 서로 가까이 기대어 조용히 이야기했다.

raw: After a silence of a few moments, during which they all looked towards him without disturbing his outward attention from the Jacobin editor, they resumed their conversation.
en: After a brief silence, during which they all stared at him without breaking his focus on the revolutionary article, they went back to their conversation.
ko: 그들 모두가 그가 혁명 기사에 집중하는 것을 깨지 않은 채 그를 응시하는 짧은 침묵 후에, 그들은 다시 대화로 돌아갔다.

raw: “It is true what madame says,” observed Jacques Three. “Why stop?
en: “What madame says is true,” Jacques Three agreed. “Why stop?
ko: “마담이 말한 것이 사실입니다.” 자크 3세가 동의했다. “왜 멈춥니까?

raw: There is great force in that.
en: There is great reason in that.
ko: 거기에는 훌륭한 이유가 있습니다.

raw: Why stop?”
en: Why stop?”
ko: 왜 멈춥니까?”

raw: “Well, well,” reasoned Defarge, “but one must stop somewhere.
en: “Well, yes,” Defarge reasoned, “but we must stop somewhere.
ko: “음, 그래,” 드파르지가 추론했다. “하지만 우리는 어딘가에서 멈춰야만 해.

raw: After all, the question is still where?”
en: After all, the question is: where?”
ko: 결국 문제는 이것이다: 어디서?”

raw: “At extermination,” said madame.
en: “At total destruction,” Madame Defarge said.
ko: “완전한 파괴에서,” 마담 드파르지가 말했다.

raw: “Magnificent!” croaked Jacques Three.
en: “Magnificent!” croaked Jacques Three.
ko: “아주 멋집니다!” 자크 3세가 쉰 소리로 말했다.

raw: The Vengeance, also, highly approved.
en: The Vengeance also strongly agreed.
ko: 복수도 강력히 동의했다.

raw: “Extermination is good doctrine, my wife,” said Defarge, rather troubled; “in general, I say nothing against it.
en: “Destroying them all is a good policy, my wife,” said Defarge, looking troubled. “Usually, I don't argue against it.
ko: “그들 모두를 파괴하는 것은 좋은 정책이야, 내 아내여,” 드파르지가 곤란한 표정을 지으며 말했다. “보통은 나도 그것에 반대하지 않아.

raw: But this Doctor has suffered much; you have seen him to-day; you have observed his face when the paper was read.”
en: But this Doctor has suffered so much. You saw him today; you saw his face when his letter was read.”
ko: 하지만 이 박사는 너무 많은 고통을 겪었어. 당신도 오늘 그를 보았지; 그의 편지가 읽혀질 때 당신도 그의 얼굴을 보았잖아.”

raw: “I have observed his face!” repeated madame, contemptuously and angrily. “Yes. I have observed his face.
en: “I saw his face!” Madame Defarge repeated angrily and scornfully. “Yes, I saw it.
ko: “그의 얼굴을 보았지!” 마담 드파르지가 화를 내며 경멸조로 반복했다. “그래, 보았어.

raw: I have observed his face to be not the face of a true friend of the Republic.
en: I saw that his face is not the face of a true friend of the Republic.
ko: 나는 그의 얼굴이 공화국의 진정한 친구의 얼굴이 아님을 보았어.

raw: Let him take care of his face!”
en: He had better watch his step!”
ko: 그는 발걸음을 조심하는 게 좋을 거야!”

raw: “And you have observed, my wife,” said Defarge, in a deprecatory manner, “the anguish of his daughter, which must be a dreadful anguish to him!”
en: “And you must have seen, my wife,” Defarge said softly, “the terrible pain of his daughter, which must be agonizing for him!”
ko: “그리고 당신도 틀림없이 보았을 거요, 내 아내여,” 드파르지가 부드럽게 말했다. “그의 딸의 끔찍한 고통을, 그것이 그에게는 참기 힘든 고통임에 틀림없소!”

raw: “I have observed his daughter,” repeated madame; “yes, I have observed his daughter, more times than one.
en: “I have watched his daughter,” Madame Defarge repeated. “Yes, I have watched her more than once.
ko: “나는 그의 딸을 지켜보았지,” 마담 드파르지가 반복했다. “그래, 나는 그녀를 한 번 이상 지켜보았어.

raw: I have observed her to-day, and I have observed her other days.
en: I saw her today, and I've seen her on other days.
ko: 나는 오늘 그녀를 보았고, 다른 날들에도 그녀를 보았어.

raw: I have observed her in the court, and I have observed her in the street by the prison.
en: I've watched her in the courtroom, and I've watched her standing in the street near the prison.
ko: 법정에서 그녀를 지켜보았고, 감옥 근처 거리에 서 있는 것도 지켜보았어.

raw: Let me but lift my finger--!” She seemed to raise it (the listener’s eyes were always on his paper), and to let it fall with a rattle on the ledge before her, as if the axe had dropped.
en: If I only lift my finger, !” She raised her finger, while Carton pretended to keep reading, and let it drop hard on the counter, making a sound like the heavy blade of the Guillotine falling.
ko: 내가 손가락을 들기만 하면, !” 그녀는 손가락을 치켜들었고, 그동안 카턴은 계속 읽는 척했으며, 그것을 카운터 위로 세게 떨어뜨려 기요틴의 무거운 칼날이 떨어지는 것 같은 소리를 냈다.

raw: “The citizeness is superb!” croaked the Juryman.
en: “The citizenness is magnificent!” croaked the juror.
ko: “시민 동지는 정말 대단합니다!” 배심원이 쉰 목소리로 말했다.

raw: “She is an Angel!” said The Vengeance, and embraced her.
en: “She is an angel!” said The Vengeance, hugging her.
ko: “그녀는 천사입니다!” 복수가 그녀를 껴안으며 말했다.

raw: “As to thee,” pursued madame, implacably, addressing her husband, “if it depended on thee--which, happily, it does not--thou wouldst rescue this man even now.”
en: “As for you,” Madame Defarge continued, looking coldly at her husband, “if it were up to you, which, thank goodness, it is not, you would save this man even now.”
ko: “당신에 대해 말하자면,” 마담 드파르지가 남편을 차갑게 바라보며 계속했다. “만약 그것이 당신에게 달려있다면, 다행히도 그렇지 않지만, 당신은 지금 당장이라도 이 남자를 구하려 할 것이오.”

raw: “No!” protested Defarge. “Not if to lift this glass would do it!
en: “No!” Defarge protested. “Not even if lifting this glass could do it!
ko: “아니!” 드파르지가 항의했다. “이 잔을 들어 올리는 것으로 그럴 수 있다 해도 그렇지 않을 거요!

raw: But I would leave the matter there.
en: But I would stop there.
ko: 하지만 나는 거기서 멈출 거요.

raw: I say, stop there.”
en: I say, let us stop with Darnay.”
ko: 내 말은, 다네이에서 멈추자는 거요.”

raw: “See you then, Jacques,” said Madame Defarge, wrathfully; “and see you, too, my little Vengeance; see you both!
en: “Listen to me, Jacques,” Madame Defarge said furiously, “and listen to me too, my little Vengeance.
ko: "자크, 내 말을 들어," 드파르지 부인이 격렬하게 말했다. "그리고 내 작은 복수, 너도 내 말을 들어."

raw: Listen!
en: Listen to both of us!
ko: 우리 둘 다의 말을 들어!

raw: For other crimes as tyrants and oppressors, I have this race a long time on my register, doomed to destruction and extermination.
en: I have had this whole family name written down in my secret register for a long time, doomed to total destruction for their crimes as cruel tyrants.
ko: 나는 이 가문 전체의 이름을 오랫동안 내 비밀 명부에 적어 두었고, 그들은 잔인한 폭군으로서 지은 죄 때문에 완전한 파멸을 맞이할 운명이다.

raw: Ask my husband, is that so.”
en: Ask my husband if that is true.”
ko: 그게 사실인지 내 남편에게 물어보라."

raw: “It is so,” assented Defarge, without being asked.
en: “It is true,” Defarge agreed, without even being asked.
ko: "사실이다," 드파르지가 묻지도 않았는데 동의했다.

raw: “In the beginning of the great days, when the Bastille falls, he finds this paper of to-day, and he brings it home, and in the middle of the night when this place is clear and shut, we read it, here on this spot, by the light of this lamp.
en: “At the start of our great revolution, when the Bastille fell, he found the letter read in court today. He brought it home, and in the middle of the night, when this shop was empty and locked, we read it right here by the light of this lamp.
ko: "우리의 위대한 혁명이 시작될 때 바스티유가 함락되었을 때, 그는 오늘 법정에서 읽힌 편지를 발견했다. 그는 그것을 집으로 가져왔고, 한밤중에 이 가게가 텅 비고 문이 잠겼을 때 우리는 이 램프 불빛에 의지해 바로 여기서 그것을 읽었다.

raw: Ask him, is that so.”
en: Ask him if that is true.”
ko: 그게 사실인지 그에게 물어보라."

raw: “It is so,” assented Defarge.
en: “It is true,” Defarge agreed.
ko: "사실이다," 드파르지가 동의했다.

raw: “That night, I tell him, when the paper is read through, and the lamp is burnt out, and the day is gleaming in above those shutters and between those iron bars, that I have now a secret to communicate.
en: “That night, when we finished reading the paper and the lamp went out, as daylight started shining through the shutters and bars, I told him I had a secret to share.
ko: "그날 밤, 우리가 종이를 다 읽고 램프가 꺼졌을 때 덧문과 창살 사이로 여명이 비치기 시작하면서, 나는 그에게 털어놓을 비밀이 있다고 말했다.

raw: Ask him, is that so.”
en: Ask him if that is true.”
ko: 그게 사실인지 그에게 물어보라."

raw: “It is so,” assented Defarge again.
en: “It is true,” Defarge agreed again.
ko: "사실이다," 드파르지가 다시 동의했다.

raw: “I communicate to him that secret.
en: “I told him that secret.
ko: "내가 그에게 그 비밀을 말했다.

raw: I smite this bosom with these two hands as I smite it now, and I tell him, ‘Defarge, I was brought up among the fishermen of the sea-shore, and that peasant family so injured by the two Evrémonde brothers, as that Bastille paper describes, is my family.
en: I beat my chest with my hands, just as I do now, and I told him, ‘Defarge, I was raised among seashore fishermen. That peasant family so horribly treated by the Evrémonde brothers, which the Bastille letter describes, was _my_ family.
ko: 나는 지금 내가 하는 것처럼 내 손으로 가슴을 치며 그에게 말했다. '드파르지, 나는 바닷가 어부들 사이에서 자랐다. 바스티유 편지에 묘사된 에브레몽드 형제에게 그토록 끔찍한 취급을 받은 그 농부 가족이 바로 _나의_ 가족이었다.

raw: Defarge, that sister of the mortally wounded boy upon the ground was my sister, that husband was my sister’s husband, that unborn child was their child, that brother was my brother, that father was my father, those dead are my dead, and that summons to answer for those things descends to me!’ Ask him, is that so.”
en: Defarge, that sister of the dying boy on the ground was my sister. Her husband was my brother-in-law. Their unborn child was my niece or nephew. That boy was my brother, that father was my father. Those dead are my dead, and it is up to me to make sure those crimes are answered for!’ Ask him if that is true.”
ko: 드파르지, 땅에서 죽어가는 소년의 누이는 내 언니였다. 그녀의 남편은 내 형부였다. 그들의 태어나지 않은 아이는 내 조카였다. 그 소년은 내 오빠였고, 그 아버지는 내 아버지였다. 그 죽은 이들은 나의 죽은 이들이고, 그 범죄에 대한 대가를 치르게 하는 것은 나에게 달려 있다!' 그게 사실인지 그에게 물어보라."

raw: “It is so,” assented Defarge once more.
en: “It is true,” Defarge agreed once more.
ko: "사실이다," 드파르지가 한 번 더 동의했다.

raw: “Then tell Wind and Fire where to stop,” returned madame; “but don’t tell me.”
en: “Then go tell the Wind and the Fire where to stop,” Madame Defarge replied, “but do not tell me.”
ko: "그럼 가서 바람과 불에게 어디서 멈추라고 말해라," 드파르지 부인이 대답했다, "하지만 나에게는 말하지 마라."

raw: Both her hearers derived a horrible enjoyment from the deadly nature of her wrath--the listener could feel how white she was, without seeing her--and both highly commended it.
en: Both of her listeners took a dark pleasure in her deadly anger, Carton could tell how pale and intense she was, even without looking at her, and both praised her.
ko: 두 청취자는 그녀의 치명적인 분노에 어두운 쾌감을 느꼈고, 카턴은 그녀를 보지 않고도 그녀가 얼마나 창백하고 강렬한지 알 수 있었으며, 두 사람은 그녀를 칭찬했다.

raw: Defarge, a weak minority, interposed a few words for the memory of the compassionate wife of the Marquis; but only elicited from his own wife a repetition of her last reply. “Tell the Wind and the Fire where to stop; not me!”
en: Defarge, standing alone, tried to say a few words in memory of the kind wife of the Marquis, but his wife only repeated her response: “Tell the Wind and the Fire where to stop; not me!”
ko: 드파르지는 혼자 서서 친절한 후작 부인을 추억하며 몇 마디 하려 했으나 그의 아내는 그녀의 대답만을 반복할 뿐이었다. "바람과 불에게 어디서 멈추라고 말하라. 나에게는 말고!"

raw: Customers entered, and the group was broken up.
en: More customers entered, and the group split up.
ko: 더 많은 손님이 들어왔고 일행은 흩어졌다.

raw: The English customer paid for what he had had, perplexedly counted his change, and asked, as a stranger, to be directed towards the National Palace.
en: The English customer paid for his wine, pretended to struggle to count his change, and asked for directions to the National Palace.
ko: 영국인 손님은 포도주값을 치르고, 거스름돈을 세는 데 애먹는 척하며, 국민 궁전으로 가는 길을 물었다.

raw: Madame Defarge took him to the door, and put her arm on his, in pointing out the road.
en: Madame Defarge walked him to the door, placing her hand on his arm to point down the street.
ko: 드파르지 부인은 그의 팔에 손을 얹고 거리를 가리키며 문까지 그를 배웅했다.

raw: The English customer was not without his reflections then, that it might be a good deed to seize that arm, lift it, and strike under it sharp and deep.
en: Carton could not help thinking that it would be a good deed to grab that arm, lift it, and plunge a knife deep into her heart.
ko: 카턴은 그 팔을 잡고 들어올려 칼을 그녀의 심장 깊숙이 찌르는 것이 좋은 일일 것이라는 생각을 지울 수 없었다.

raw: But, he went his way, and was soon swallowed up in the shadow of the prison wall.
en: But he walked away and was soon lost in the shadow of the prison wall.
ko: 그러나 그는 걸어 나갔고 곧 감옥 벽의 그림자 속으로 사라졌다.

raw: At the appointed hour, he emerged from it to present himself in Mr.
en: At the agreed time, he left the darkness and went to Mr.
ko: 약속한 시간에 그는 어둠을 떠나 로리 씨에게로 갔다.

raw: Lorry’s room again, where he found the old gentleman walking to and fro in restless anxiety.
en: Lorry's room, where he found the old gentleman pacing back and forth in great worry.
ko: 로리 씨의 방에서 그는 그 나이 든 신사가 큰 걱정에 싸여 앞뒤로 서성이는 것을 발견했다.

raw: He said he had been with Lucie until just now, and had only left her for a few minutes, to come and keep his appointment.
en: Mr. Lorry said he had been with Lucie until just now, leaving her only to keep his meeting with Carton.
ko: 로리 씨는 방금 전까지 루시와 함께 있었으며 카턴과의 만남을 지키기 위해서만 그녀 곁을 떠났다고 말했다.

raw: Her father had not been seen, since he quitted the banking-house towards four o’clock.
en: Her father had not been seen since he left the bank around four o'clock.
ko: 그녀의 아버지는 네 시경 은행을 떠난 이후로 보이지 않았다.

raw: She had some faint hopes that his mediation might save Charles, but they were very slight.
en: Lucie had a tiny bit of hope that her father's influence might save Charles, but it was very small.
ko: 루시는 아버지의 영향력이 찰스를 구할 수 있을지도 모른다는 아주 작은 희망을 가졌지만 그것은 매우 작았다.

raw: He had been more than five hours gone: where could he be?
en: He had been gone for more than five hours; where could he be?
ko: 그는 다섯 시간 넘게 가 있었는데, 그가 어디에 있을 수 있을까?

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.
ko: 로리 씨는.

raw: Lorry waited until ten; but, Doctor Manette not returning, and he being unwilling to leave Lucie any longer, it was arranged that he should go back to her, and come to the banking-house again at midnight.
en: Lorry waited until ten o'clock. Since Dr. Manette still had not returned, and Mr. Lorry did not want to leave Lucie alone any longer, they decided that he would go back to her and return to the bank at midnight.
ko: 열 시까지 기다렸다. 마네트 박사가 여전히 돌아오지 않았고, 로리 씨는 루시를 더 이상 혼자 두고 싶지 않았기 때문에, 그가 그녀에게로 돌아가고 자정에 은행으로 돌아오기로 결정했다.

raw: In the meanwhile, Carton would wait alone by the fire for the Doctor.
en: In the meantime, Carton would wait by the fire for the Doctor.
ko: 그동안 카턴은 불 옆에서 박사를 기다리기로 했다.

raw: He waited and waited, and the clock struck twelve; but Doctor Manette did not come back.
en: Carton waited and waited until the clock struck midnight, but Dr. Manette did not return.
ko: 카턴은 시계가 자정을 칠 때까지 기다리고 또 기다렸으나 마네트 박사는 돌아오지 않았다.

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.
ko: 로리 씨가 돌아왔다.

raw: Lorry returned, and found no tidings of him, and brought none.
en: Lorry came back, having heard no news and bringing none.
ko: 아무 소식도 듣지 못하고 아무 소식도 가져오지 않은 채.

raw: Where could he be?
en: Where could the Doctor be?
ko: 박사는 어디에 있을 수 있을까?

raw: They were discussing this question, and were almost building up some weak structure of hope on his prolonged absence, when they heard him on the stairs.
en: They were discussing this and trying to find some small hope in his long absence when they heard him walking up the stairs.
ko: 그들이 이것을 논의하며 그의 긴 부재에서 어떤 작은 희망이라도 찾으려 할 때 그가 계단을 걸어 올라오는 소리가 들렸다.

raw: The instant he entered the room, it was plain that all was lost.
en: The moment he walked into the room, it was clear that all hope was gone.
ko: 그가 방에 들어온 순간 모든 희망이 사라졌다는 것이 분명했다.

raw: Whether he had really been to any one, or whether he had been all that time traversing the streets, was never known.
en: Whether he had actually met with anyone or had spent all those hours just wandering the streets was never known.
ko: 그가 실제로 누군가를 만났는지 아니면 그 모든 시간을 그저 거리를 배회하며 보냈는지는 결코 알려지지 않았다.

raw: As he stood staring at them, they asked him no question, for his face told them everything.
en: As he stood there staring at them, they did not ask any questions because his face told them everything.
ko: 그가 거기에 서서 그들을 빤히 쳐다보았을 때, 그의 얼굴이 모든 것을 말해주었기 때문에 그들은 아무 질문도 하지 않았다.

raw: “I cannot find it,” said he, “and I must have it.
en: “I can't find it,” he said, “ and I must have it.
ko: "나는 그것을 찾을 수 없어," 그가 말했다, "그리고 나는 그것을 가져야만 해.

raw: Where is it?”
en: Where is it?”
ko: 어디에 있지?"

raw: His head and throat were bare, and, as he spoke with a helpless look straying all around, he took his coat off, and let it drop on the floor.
en: His head and neck were bare, and as he spoke with a helpless, wandering look, he took off his coat and let it drop onto the floor.
ko: 그의 머리와 목은 맨 상태였고, 그가 무기력하고 방황하는 표정으로 말하면서 외투를 벗어 바닥에 떨어뜨렸다.

raw: “Where is my bench?
en: “Where is my shoemaker's bench?
ko: "내 구두 수선공 벤치는 어디에 있지?

raw: I have been looking everywhere for my bench, and I can’t find it.
en: I've been looking everywhere for my bench and I can't find it.
ko: 내 벤치를 찾아 사방을 둘러보았지만 찾을 수 없네.

raw: What have they done with my work?
en: What have they done with my work?
ko: 그들이 내 작업물로 무슨 짓을 한 거지?

raw: Time presses: I must finish those shoes.”
en: Time is running out; I must finish those shoes.”
ko: 시간이 얼마 남지 않았네; 나는 그 신발을 끝내야만 해."

raw: They looked at one another, and their hearts died within them.
en: Mr. Lorry and Carton looked at each other, their hearts sinking.
ko: 로리 씨와 카턴은 서로를 바라보았고 그들의 가슴은 철렁 내려앉았다.

raw: “Come, come!” said he, in a whimpering miserable way; “let me get to work.
en: “Come on, come on!” Dr. Manette whimpered in a miserable voice. “Let me get to work.
ko: "어서, 어서!" 마네트 박사가 비참한 목소리로 훌쩍거렸다. "내가 일을 하게 해 주게.

raw: Give me my work.”
en: Give me my tools.”
ko: 내 도구를 주게."

raw: Receiving no answer, he tore his hair, and beat his feet upon the ground, like a distracted child.
en: When they did not answer, he pulled his hair and stamped his feet on the ground like a panicked child.
ko: 그들이 대답하지 않자, 그는 당황한 아이처럼 자신의 머리카락을 쥐어뜯고 땅에 발을 굴렀다.

raw: “Don’t torture a poor forlorn wretch,” he implored them, with a dreadful cry; “but give me my work!
en: “Don't torture a poor, miserable man,” he begged with a terrible cry. “Just give me my work!
ko: "가엾고 비참한 사람을 고문하지 마," 그가 끔찍한 울부짖음과 함께 애원했다. "그저 내 일거리를 주게!

raw: What is to become of us, if those shoes are not done to-night?”
en: What will happen to us if these shoes are not finished tonight?”
ko: 이 신발을 오늘 밤까지 끝내지 못하면 우리는 어떻게 되는 건가?"

raw: Lost, utterly lost!
en: He was lost, completely lost!
ko: 그는 길을 잃었다, 완전히 길을 잃었다!

raw: It was so clearly beyond hope to reason with him, or try to restore him, that--as if by agreement--they each put a hand upon his shoulder, and soothed him to sit down before the fire, with a promise that he should have his work presently.
en: It was so obviously useless to argue with him or try to bring him back to his senses that, as if they had agreed without speaking, they each placed a hand on his shoulder and gently guided him to sit by the fire, promising that he would have his work soon.
ko: 그와 논쟁하거나 그를 다시 이성으로 되돌리려 하는 것은 명백히 소용없는 일이었으므로, 그들은 말없이 동의한 듯 각자 그의 어깨에 손을 얹고 부드럽게 그를 이끌어 불 옆에 앉히며 곧 일거리를 갖게 될 것이라고 약속했다.

raw: He sank into the chair, and brooded over the embers, and shed tears.
en: He sank into the chair, staring sadly at the hot coals and crying.
ko: 그는 의자에 주저앉아, 뜨거운 숯불을 슬프게 바라보며 울었다.

raw: As if all that had happened since the garret time were a momentary fancy, or a dream, Mr.
en: It was as if everything that had happened since his release from the attic room in Paris was just a passing dream; Mr.
ko: 그가 파리의 다락방에서 풀려난 이후로 일어난 모든 일이 마치 스쳐가는 꿈인 것 같았다. 로리 씨는 그가 드파르지가 처음 그를 가두어두었을 때와 똑같은 무너진 상태로 오그라드는 것을 보았다.

raw: Lorry saw him shrink into the exact figure that Defarge had had in keeping.
en: Lorry saw him shrink back into the exact same broken state he was in when Defarge first kept him.
ko: 로리 씨는.

raw: Affected, and impressed with terror as they both were, by this spectacle of ruin, it was not a time to yield to such emotions.
en: Although they were both deeply moved and terrified by this sight of his mental collapse, it was not a time to give in to sadness.
ko: 비록 그들 두 사람은 그의 정신적 붕괴의 광경에 깊이 감동하고 겁에 질렸지만, 지금은 슬픔에 굴복할 때가 아니었다.

raw: His lonely daughter, bereft of her final hope and reliance, appealed to them both too strongly.
en: His poor daughter, now stripped of her last hope and support, needed them too much.
ko: 그의 불쌍한 딸이 이제 마지막 희망과 버팀목마저 빼앗긴 채 그들을 너무나 필요로 했다.

raw: Again, as if by agreement, they looked at one another with one meaning in their faces.
en: Again, as if by silent agreement, they looked at each other with the same thought in their minds.
ko: 다시, 침묵의 동의라도 한 듯 그들은 같은 생각을 마음에 품고 서로를 쳐다보았다.

raw: Carton was the first to speak:
en: Carton spoke first:
ko: 카턴이 먼저 입을 열었다:

raw: “The last chance is gone: it was not much.
en: “The last chance is gone; it wasn't much anyway.
ko: "마지막 기회는 사라졌습니다. 어쨌든 별것 아니었지만요.

raw: Yes; he had better be taken to her.
en: Yes, he had better be taken back to Lucie.
ko: 네, 그를 루시에게 다시 데려가는 편이 낫겠습니다.

raw: But, before you go, will you, for a moment, steadily attend to me?
en: But before you go, will you listen to me carefully for a moment?
ko: 하지만 가시기 전에 잠시만 제 말을 주의 깊게 들어 주시겠습니까?

raw: Don’t ask me why I make the stipulations I am going to make, and exact the promise I am going to exact; I have a reason--a good one.”
en: Don't ask me why I am making these demands, or why I need you to promise what I'm about to ask. I have a reason, a very good one.”
ko: 제가 왜 이런 요구를 하는지, 왜 제가 부탁하려는 것을 당신이 약속해 주어야 하는지 묻지 마십시오. 저에게는 이유가 있습니다, 아주 타당한 이유가요."

raw: “I do not doubt it,” answered Mr.
en: “I don't doubt it,” Mr.
ko: "나는 그것을 의심하지 않네," 로리 씨가 대답했다.

raw: Lorry. “Say on.”
en: Lorry replied. “Tell me.”
ko: "말해보게."

raw: The figure in the chair between them, was all the time monotonously rocking itself to and fro, and moaning.
en: The broken doctor sat in the chair between them, rocking back and forth and moaning.
ko: 무너진 박사는 그들 사이의 의자에 앉아 앞뒤로 몸을 흔들며 신음하고 있었다.

raw: They spoke in such a tone as they would have used if they had been watching by a sick-bed in the night.
en: They spoke in the quiet tones people use when watching over a sickbed in the middle of the night.
ko: 그들은 한밤중에 병상을 지키는 사람들이 사용하는 조용한 목소리로 말했다.

raw: Carton stooped to pick up the coat, which lay almost entangling his feet.
en: Carton bent down to pick up the Doctor's coat, which was lying near his feet.
ko: 카턴은 몸을 굽혀 그의 발 근처에 놓여 있던 박사의 외투를 집어들었다.

raw: As he did so, a small case in which the Doctor was accustomed to carry the lists of his day’s duties, fell lightly on the floor.
en: As he did, a small leather case that the Doctor used to carry his daily schedule fell onto the floor.
ko: 그가 그러자, 박사가 일일 일정을 지니고 다니던 작은 가죽 지갑이 바닥에 떨어졌다.

raw: Carton took it up, and there was a folded paper in it. “We should look at this!” he said.
en: Carton picked it up and found a folded paper inside. “We should look at this!” he said.
ko: 카턴은 그것을 집어들었고 그 안에 접힌 종이가 있는 것을 발견했다. "우리는 이것을 봐야 합니다!" 그가 말했다.

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.
ko: 로리 씨는.

raw: Lorry nodded his consent.
en: Lorry nodded.
ko: 고개를 끄덕였다.

raw: He opened it, and exclaimed, “Thank _God!_”
en: Carton opened it and exclaimed, “Thank _God_!”
ko: 카턴이 그것을 열고 외쳤다, "_하나님_ 맙소사!"

raw: “What is it?” asked Mr.
en: “What is it?” Mr.
ko: "무엇인가?" 로리 씨가 간절하게 물었다.

raw: Lorry, eagerly.
en: Lorry asked eagerly.
ko: 로리 씨는.

raw: “A moment!
en: “Just a moment!
ko: "잠시만요!

raw: Let me speak of it in its place.
en: Let me explain that in a second.
ko: 그것은 잠시 후에 설명하겠습니다.

raw: First,” he put his hand in his coat, and took another paper from it, “that is the certificate which enables me to pass out of this city.
en: First,” he reached into his coat and pulled out another paper, “this is the travel pass that allows me to leave the city.
ko: 먼저," 그는 외투 안으로 손을 뻗어 다른 종이를 꺼냈다. "이것은 내가 도시를 떠날 수 있게 해주는 여행 통행증입니다.

raw: Look at it.
en: Look at it.
ko: 보세요.

raw: You see--Sydney Carton, an Englishman?”
en: You see, Sydney Carton, an Englishman?”
ko: 보이시죠, 영국인 시드니 카턴?"

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.
ko: 로리 씨는.

raw: Lorry held it open in his hand, gazing in his earnest face.
en: Lorry held it open, looking at Carton's serious face.
ko: 그것을 들고 펴서 카턴의 심각한 얼굴을 바라보았다.

raw: “Keep it for me until to-morrow.
en: “Keep it for me until tomorrow.
ko: "내일까지 그것을 나를 위해 보관해 주십시오.

raw: I shall see him to-morrow, you remember, and I had better not take it into the prison.”
en: Remember, I am going to see Charles tomorrow, and it is better if I don't bring this pass into the prison.”
ko: 기억하십시오, 나는 내일 찰스를 만나러 갈 것이고, 감옥에 이 통행증을 가져가지 않는 편이 낫습니다."

raw: “Why not?”
en: “Why not?”
ko: "왜 안 되는가?"

raw: “I don’t know; I prefer not to do so.
en: “I'm not sure; I just prefer not to.
ko: "확실하지는 않지만 그저 그러지 않는 것이 좋겠습니다.

raw: Now, take this paper that Doctor Manette has carried about him.
en: Now, take this paper that Doctor Manette had on him.
ko: 이제, 마네트 박사가 가지고 있던 이 종이를 가져가십시오.

raw: It is a similar certificate, enabling him and his daughter and her child, at any time, to pass the barrier and the frontier!
en: It is a similar travel pass, allowing him, his daughter, and her child to pass through the city gates and cross the border at any time!
ko: 그것은 그와 그의 딸, 그리고 그녀의 아이가 언제든지 성문을 통과하고 국경을 넘을 수 있도록 허가하는 비슷한 여행 통행증입니다!

raw: You see?”
en: You see?”
ko: 아시겠습니까?"

raw: “Yes!”
en: “Yes!”
ko: "그래!"

raw: “Perhaps he obtained it as his last and utmost precaution against evil, yesterday.
en: “Perhaps he got it yesterday as a final precaution.
ko: "아마도 그는 마지막 예방책으로 어제 그것을 구했을 것입니다.

raw: When is it dated?
en: When is it dated?
ko: 날짜가 언제로 되어 있습니까?

raw: But no matter; don’t stay to look; put it up carefully with mine and your own.
en: Actually, it doesn't matter; don't waste time looking now. Put it away safely with mine and yours.
ko: 사실 그것은 중요하지 않습니다. 지금 확인하느라 시간을 낭비하지 마십시오. 그것을 당신의 것과 나의 것과 함께 안전하게 넣어 두십시오.

raw: Now, observe!
en: Listen carefully!
ko: 주의 깊게 들으십시오!

raw: I never doubted until within this hour or two, that he had, or could have such a paper.
en: I didn't know until a couple of hours ago that he even had such a paper.
ko: 나는 불과 몇 시간 전까지 그가 그런 종이를 가지고 있다는 사실조차 몰랐습니다.

raw: It is good, until recalled.
en: It is valid until it is canceled.
ko: 그것은 취소될 때까지 유효합니다.

raw: But it may be soon recalled, and, I have reason to think, will be.”
en: But it might be canceled very soon, and I have reason to believe it will be.”
ko: 하지만 그것은 아주 곧 취소될지도 모르며, 나는 그렇게 될 것이라고 믿을 만한 이유가 있습니다."

raw: “They are not in danger?”
en: “Are they in danger?”
ko: “그들이 위험에 처했나요?”

raw: “They are in great danger.
en: “They are in extreme danger.
ko: “그들은 극도의 위험에 처해 있습니다.

raw: They are in danger of denunciation by Madame Defarge.
en: They are about to be accused by Madame Defarge.
ko: 그들은 마담 드파르지에게 고발당할 것입니다.

raw: I know it from her own lips.
en: I know it because I heard it from her own mouth tonight.
ko: 오늘 밤 그녀의 입으로 직접 들었기 때문에 알고 있습니다.

raw: I have overheard words of that woman’s, to-night, which have presented their danger to me in strong colours.
en: What I overheard showed me their danger in terrifying detail.
ko: 내가 엿들은 내용은 그들의 위험을 끔찍할 정도로 상세히 보여주었습니다.

raw: I have lost no time, and since then, I have seen the spy.
en: I didn't waste any time, and since then I have met with Barsad the spy.
ko: 나는 시간을 낭비하지 않았고, 그 이후로 스파이인 바사드를 만났습니다.

raw: He confirms me.
en: He confirmed it.
ko: 그가 그것을 확인해주었습니다.

raw: He knows that a wood-sawyer, living by the prison wall, is under the control of the Defarges, and has been rehearsed by Madame Defarge as to his having seen Her”--he never mentioned Lucie’s name--“making signs and signals to prisoners.
en: He knows that a wood-cutter living by the prison wall is controlled by the Defarges, and that Madame Defarge has coached him to testify that he saw her”, he avoided saying Lucie's name, “making signals to the prisoners.
ko: 그는 감옥 벽 옆에 사는 나무꾼이 드파르지 부부의 통제를 받고 있으며, 마담 드파르지가 그 나무꾼에게 그녀가 죄수들에게 신호를 보내는 것을 보았다고 증언하도록 지시했다는 것을 알고 있습니다”, 그는 루시의 이름을 언급하기를 피했다.

raw: It is easy to foresee that the pretence will be the common one, a prison plot, and that it will involve her life--and perhaps her child’s--and perhaps her father’s--for both have been seen with her at that place.
en: It is easy to see that they will accuse her of plotting a prison escape. It will cost her life, and probably her child's, and her father's too, since both have been seen with her near the prison.
ko: 그들이 그녀를 탈옥 모의 혐의로 고발할 것이라는 점은 쉽게 알 수 있습니다. 그것은 그녀의 목숨뿐만 아니라, 감옥 근처에서 그녀와 함께 있는 것이 목격되었기 때문에 아마도 그녀의 아이와 아버지의 목숨까지 앗아갈 것입니다.

raw: Don’t look so horrified.
en: Don't look so horrified.
ko: 너무 겁먹은 표정 짓지 마십시오.

raw: You will save them all.”
en: You are going to save them all.”
ko: 당신이 그들 모두를 구할 것입니다.”

raw: “Heaven grant I may, Carton!
en: “May God help me do it, Carton!
ko: “신께서 내가 그렇게 하도록 도와주시기를, 카턴!

raw: But how?”
en: But how?”
ko: 하지만 어떻게 말입니까?”

raw: “I am going to tell you how.
en: “I am going to tell you how.
ko: “어떻게 할지 말씀드리겠습니다.

raw: It will depend on you, and it could depend on no better man.
en: It will all depend on you, and there is no better man for the job.
ko: 모든 것은 당신에게 달려 있으며, 이 일에 당신보다 더 적임자는 없습니다.

raw: This new denunciation will certainly not take place until after to-morrow; probably not until two or three days afterwards; more probably a week afterwards.
en: This new accusation won't happen until after tomorrow, probably not for two or three days, or even a week.
ko: 이 새로운 고발은 내일이 지나기 전에는 일어나지 않을 것이며, 아마도 2~3일, 어쩌면 일주일 동안은 일어나지 않을 것입니다.

raw: You know it is a capital crime, to mourn for, or sympathise with, a victim of the Guillotine.
en: You know that it is a crime punishable by death to mourn for or show sympathy for anyone executed by the Guillotine.
ko: 단두대에서 처형된 사람을 애도하거나 동정하는 것은 사형에 처해질 수 있는 범죄라는 것을 당신도 알고 계실 것입니다.

raw: She and her father would unquestionably be guilty of this crime, and this woman (the inveteracy of whose pursuit cannot be described) would wait to add that strength to her case, and make herself doubly sure.
en: Lucie and her father will definitely show their grief, and Madame Defarge, who will never stop hunting them, will wait for that to happen to make her case even stronger and doubly sure.
ko: 루시와 그녀의 아버지는 분명히 슬픔을 보일 것이고, 그들을 사냥하는 것을 결코 멈추지 않을 마담 드파르지는 자신의 주장을 더욱 강력하고 확실하게 만들기 위해 그 일이 일어나기를 기다릴 것입니다.

raw: You follow me?”
en: Do you understand?”
ko: 이해하시겠습니까?”

raw: “So attentively, and with so much confidence in what you say, that for the moment I lose sight,” touching the back of the Doctor’s chair, “even of this distress.”
en: “I am listening so closely, and with so much trust in you, that for a moment,” Mr. Lorry said, touching the back of the Doctor's chair, “I even forgot about this terrible situation.”
ko: “너무나 주의 깊게 듣고 있고 당신을 매우 신뢰하고 있어서, 잠시 동안은” 박사의 의자 등받이를 만지며 로리 씨가 말했다. “이 끔찍한 상황조차 잊고 있었습니다.”

raw: “You have money, and can buy the means of travelling to the seacoast as quickly as the journey can be made.
en: “You have money, and you can buy carriage passage to the coast as fast as possible.
ko: “당신은 돈이 있으니, 해안으로 가는 마차표를 최대한 빨리 살 수 있습니다.

raw: Your preparations have been completed for some days, to return to England.
en: You have already finished your preparations to return to England.
ko: 당신은 이미 영국으로 돌아갈 준비를 마쳤습니다.

raw: Early to-morrow have your horses ready, so that they may be in starting trim at two o’clock in the afternoon.”
en: Early tomorrow, have your horses and carriage ready so they are set to leave at two o'clock in the afternoon.”
ko: 내일 일찍, 오후 2시에 떠날 수 있도록 말과 마차를 준비해 두십시오.”

raw: “It shall be done!”
en: “It will be done!”
ko: “그렇게 하겠습니다!”

raw: His manner was so fervent and inspiring, that Mr.
en: Carton's manner was so passionate and inspiring that Mr.
ko: 카턴의 태도가 너무나 열정적이고 고무적이어서

raw: Lorry caught the flame, and was as quick as youth.
en: Lorry caught his excitement, moving as quickly as a young man.
ko: 로리 씨는 그의 흥분에 전염되어 젊은이처럼 재빠르게 움직였다.

raw: “You are a noble heart.
en: “You have a noble heart.
ko: “당신은 고결한 마음을 가졌습니다.

raw: Did I say we could depend upon no better man?
en: Did I say we could depend on no better man?
ko: 우리가 이보다 더 나은 사람에게 의지할 수 없다고 제가 말했습니까?

raw: Tell her, to-night, what you know of her danger as involving her child and her father.
en: Tonight, tell her about the danger to her child and her father.
ko: 오늘 밤, 그녀에게 그녀의 아이와 아버지에게 닥친 위험에 대해 말씀하십시오.

raw: Dwell upon that, for she would lay her own fair head beside her husband’s cheerfully.” He faltered for an instant; then went on as before. “For the sake of her child and her father, press upon her the necessity of leaving Paris, with them and you, at that hour.
en: Focus on that, because she would gladly die with her husband if it were just her own life at stake.” He paused for a second, then went on. “For the sake of her child and her father, convince her that she must leave Paris with them and you at that exact hour.
ko: 그 점에 집중하십시오. 만약 그녀 자신의 목숨만 걸려 있다면 그녀는 기꺼이 남편과 함께 죽을 것이기 때문입니다.” 그는 잠시 말을 멈춘 뒤 계속했다. “그녀의 아이와 아버지를 위해서라도, 그 정확한 시간에 그녀가 그들 그리고 당신과 함께 파리를 떠나야만 한다고 그녀를 설득하십시오.

raw: Tell her that it was her husband’s last arrangement.
en: Tell her it was her husband's last request.
ko: 그것이 남편의 마지막 부탁이었다고 말씀하십시오.

raw: Tell her that more depends upon it than she dare believe, or hope.
en: Tell her that more depends on this than she can possibly imagine.
ko: 그녀가 상상할 수 있는 것보다 더 많은 것이 이 일에 달려 있다고 말씀하십시오.

raw: You think that her father, even in this sad state, will submit himself to her; do you not?”
en: You believe her father, even in this broken state, will do whatever she asks, don't you?”
ko: 당신은 그녀의 아버지가 이렇게 무너진 상태에서도 그녀가 부탁하는 것은 무엇이든 할 것이라고 믿으시지요?”

raw: “I am sure of it.”
en: “I am sure of it.”
ko: “확신합니다.”

raw: “I thought so.
en: “I thought so.
ko: “그럴 줄 알았습니다.

raw: Quietly and steadily have all these arrangements made in the courtyard here, even to the taking of your own seat in the carriage.
en: Quietly and steadily make all these arrangements here in the courtyard, even sitting in your seat in the carriage.
ko: 조용하고 차분하게 이곳 안뜰에서, 심지어 마차의 당신 자리에 앉아서 이 모든 준비를 하십시오.

raw: The moment I come to you, take me in, and drive away.”
en: The moment I come to you, pull me in and drive away.”
ko: 제가 당신에게 가는 순간, 저를 끌어당겨 태우고 출발하십시오.”

raw: “I understand that I wait for you under all circumstances?”
en: “So I must wait for you, no matter what happens?”
ko: “그러면 무슨 일이 있어도 당신을 기다려야 합니까?”

raw: “You have my certificate in your hand with the rest, you know, and will reserve my place.
en: “You have my travel pass with the others, and you will save my seat.
ko: “당신은 다른 사람들의 것과 함께 제 통행증도 가지고 있고, 제 자리도 맡아두실 겁니다.

raw: Wait for nothing but to have my place occupied, and then for England!”
en: Wait for nothing except for me to get into that seat, and then drive straight for England!”
ko: 제가 그 자리에 타는 것 외에는 아무것도 기다리지 마시고, 바로 영국을 향해 출발하십시오!”

raw: “Why, then,” said Mr.
en: “Well, then,” said Mr.
ko: “그렇다면,” 하고

raw: Lorry, grasping his eager but so firm and steady hand, “it does not all depend on one old man, but I shall have a young and ardent man at my side.”
en: Lorry, gripping Carton's eager but steady hand, “it won't all depend on one old man. I will have a young, passionate man at my side.”
ko: 카턴의 열렬하면서도 굳건한 손을 꽉 잡으며 로리 씨가 말했다. “모든 것이 늙은이 한 사람에게만 달려 있지는 않을 겁니다. 내 곁에는 젊고 열정적인 청년이 있을 테니까요.”

raw: “By the help of Heaven you shall!
en: “With Heaven's help, you will!
ko: “하늘의 도움으로, 그렇게 되실 겁니다!

raw: Promise me solemnly that nothing will influence you to alter the course on which we now stand pledged to one another.”
en: Promise me solemnly that nothing will make you change the plan we have just agreed to.”
ko: 우리가 방금 동의한 계획을 어떠한 일에도 바꾸지 않겠다고 저에게 엄숙히 약속해 주십시오.”

raw: “Nothing, Carton.”
en: “Nothing, Carton.”
ko: “어떤 일에도 바꾸지 않겠습니다, 카턴.”

raw: “Remember these words to-morrow: change the course, or delay in it--for any reason--and no life can possibly be saved, and many lives must inevitably be sacrificed.”
en: “Remember these words tomorrow: if you change the plan, or delay it for any reason, no one can be saved, and many lives will be lost.”
ko: “내일 이 말을 기억하십시오. 만약 당신이 계획을 바꾸거나 어떤 이유로든 지연시킨다면, 아무도 구할 수 없을 것이며 많은 목숨을 잃게 될 것입니다.”

raw: “I will remember them.
en: “I will remember them.
ko: “기억하겠습니다.

raw: I hope to do my part faithfully.”
en: I hope to do my part faithfully.”
ko: 내 역할을 충실히 해내기를 바랍니다.”

raw: “And I hope to do mine.
en: “And I hope to do mine.
ko: “그리고 저도 제 역할을 다하기를 바랍니다.

raw: Now, good bye!”
en: Now, goodbye!”
ko: 이제, 안녕히 계십시오!”

raw: Though he said it with a grave smile of earnestness, and though he even put the old man’s hand to his lips, he did not part from him then.
en: Although he said this with a serious, earnest smile, and even kissed the old man's hand, he did not leave him just yet.
ko: 그는 진지하고 진심 어린 미소를 지으며 이 말을 했고 노인의 손에 입을 맞추기까지 했지만, 아직 그를 떠나지 않았다.

raw: He helped him so far to arouse the rocking figure before the dying embers, as to get a cloak and hat put upon it, and to tempt it forth to find where the bench and work were hidden that it still moaningly besought to have.
en: He helped Mr. Lorry wake up the rocking doctor by the dying fire, putting a coat and hat on him, and leading him outside under the pretense of finding the shoemaker's bench and tools he kept crying for.
ko: 그는 꺼져가는 불 옆에서 몸을 흔들고 있는 박사를 로리 씨가 깨우는 것을 도왔고, 그에게 코트를 입히고 모자를 씌운 뒤, 박사가 계속해서 울며 찾는 제화공의 작업대와 도구들을 찾아주겠다는 구실로 그를 밖으로 이끌었다.

raw: He walked on the other side of it and protected it to the courtyard of the house where the afflicted heart--so happy in the memorable time when he had revealed his own desolate heart to it--outwatched the awful night.
en: Carton walked on the other side of him, protecting the broken doctor all the way back to the courtyard of the house where Lucie, who had been so happy back when Carton first confessed his lonely heart to her, was staying awake through this terrible night.
ko: 카턴은 그의 반대편에서 걸으며, 자신이 처음 그녀에게 외로운 마음을 고백했을 때 무척이나 행복해했던 루시가 이 끔찍한 밤을 지새우고 있는 집의 안뜰로 돌아가는 내내 무너진 박사를 보호했다.

raw: He entered the courtyard and remained there for a few moments alone, looking up at the light in the window of her room.
en: He entered the courtyard and stood alone for a few moments, looking up at the light in her window.
ko: 그는 안뜰로 들어가 그녀의 창문에 비친 불빛을 올려다보며 잠시 홀로 서 있었다.

raw: Before he went away, he breathed a blessing towards it, and a Farewell.
en: Before he walked away, he whispered a blessing toward the window, and a final goodbye.
ko: 그는 걸음을 옮기기 전에 창문을 향해 축복과 마지막 작별 인사를 속삭였다.
